name: gobuster
one_line: directory, DNS and virtual-host brute forcer
plain: `gobuster` guesses names. Give it a wordlist and a target and it tries every word to see what exists: directories and files on a website, subdomains of a domain, or virtual hosts on a server.
A 200 or 301 reply means the thing exists; a 404 means it does not. Hidden pages like /admin, /backup or /secret are often the way into a CTF web target.
It works in modes: dir (web paths), dns (subdomains), vhost (virtual hosts), s3 and fuzz.
when: Find hidden directories and files on a web server.
Find virtual hosts that share one IP.
Look for backup, config or admin files by extension.

examples.title: Find directories
examples.explain: dir mode tries every word as a path. Hits print with their status code and size.

examples.title: Also try file extensions
examples.explain: -x adds each extension to each word, so it finds admin.php or config.bak as well.

examples.title: Only show certain status codes
examples.explain: -s sets the codes that count as hits; -b '' clears the default blacklist (404) so you control it.

examples.title: Go faster
examples.explain: -t sets threads (parallel requests). Raise it on a lab server, lower it on a fragile one.

examples.title: Find subdomains
examples.explain: Tries word.example.com for each word and reports the ones that resolve.

examples.title: Find virtual hosts
examples.explain: Sends requests to the same IP with different Host headers; a different response reveals another site.

examples.title: Authenticated or with a cookie
examples.explain: -c sends a cookie so you can enumerate pages behind a login.

options.plain: Mode: find directories and files on a web server.
Mode: replace the word FUZZ anywhere in the URL or body.
Modes for cloud buckets and TFTP.
Status codes that count as found.
Continue even if the server answers everything (dns).
Append the domain to each word (vhost).
Help for the tool or a mode.

mistakes: Using one wordlist and calling it done: try a bigger one if nothing appears.
Reading a wildcard site: every path says 200. Compare lengths and use --exclude-length.
Using too many threads on a small lab target and crashing it.
Forgetting the trailing path or scheme in -u (needs http:// or https://).
try: Find /admin on a lab web server with common.txt.
Run again with -x php,txt and compare.
Run the dns mode on a domain you own.
see_also: ffuf(1), dirb(1), dirbuster, wfuzz(1), nikto(1), curl(1), and the wordlists in /usr/share/wordlists and /usr/share/seclists.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
